rungs.note: Definitional consistency check: the variants use the same objects as the main statement, with no cast or reindexing.

rungs.title: The cycle-class and Hodge-class constructions pinned at the upstream commit, with the upstream normalization theorems
rungs.note: Definitional pins (rfl) for each step of the upstream construction: local class normalized to pair to 1 with the complex orientation, glued on the smooth locus, extended by purity, support forgotten, ℚ-span over points of coheight p; and the Hodge side F^p ∩ conj F^p. A change upstream breaks the build here. The three upstream theorems encode the normalization (pairs to 1), non-degeneracy of the oriented local class, and chart independence under holomorphic germs. Documented in docs/cycle-class.md.

rungs.title: The known half and the equality forms, stated on upstream definitions: cycle classes are Hodge classes; Hdg^p = span; Hdg^1 = span
rungs.note: Upstream states only the inclusions. These are the targets of decision 0004; they are statements on upstream definitions, not restatements of the upstream conjecture.

rungs.title: Each equality form is the upstream inclusion together with the known half
rungs.note: HodgeConjectureEquality ↔ HodgeConjecture ∧ CycleClassesAreHodge; LefschetzOneOneEquality ↔ LefschetzOneOne ∧ CycleClassesAreHodgeOne.

rungs.title: Independent build and axiom audit of the upstream Lefschetz (1,1) proof (PR #228 head c7d5c94b)
rungs.note: Reproduced 2026-11-24: builds (5,519 jobs), upstream axiom gate passes, direct axiom print shows only the standard three, and a positive control confirms a hidden sorry would be reported. Checked at the upstream commit, not at this repository's pin; the pinned cycle class differs by a nonzero scalar (red-team record), so the identities need divisor-chern-exact.

rungs.title: Non-vacuity tests for the upstream definitions: a variety satisfying the hypotheses, a nonzero class in H^2, a nonzero cycle class
rungs.note: Rules out a definitional accident that would make Lefschetz (1,1) or the conjecture trivially true. Exact list from the red-team audit of the upstream proof; contributed upstream to Other/ where upstream wants it. The equality rungs (lefschetz-1-1-equality, cycle-classes-are-hodge, projective-space-test) are the strongest non-vacuity tests; this rung keeps the cheap ones (a variety meeting the hypotheses; a nonzero point class).

rungs.title: Port the upstream Lefschetz (1,1) stack from v4.33.1 to the current upstream pin
rungs.note: Stack: upstream PRs #217-#226, #9, #230 (Oka proper GAGA, 372 modules), #228. Contributed upstream; coordinate with the upstream authors before starting, since upstream proposed taking Oka as a dependency instead of vendoring it. Requirement (decision 0004): the port proves the divisor–Chern identity exactly on the pinned cycle class with the sign determined (rung divisor-chern-exact); a bridge 'up to a nonzero scalar' does not satisfy it. Progress 2026-11-24: parts 1–8 of 11 (191 modules, including the exact bridge to main's cycle class) build at the current pin in the staging library port/LefschetzPort; log in docs/port-lefschetz.md.

rungs.title: Lefschetz (1,1): the upstream LefschetzOneOne, checked at this repository's pin
rungs.note: Upstream's LefschetzOneOne (the inclusion Hdg^1 ≤ span), checked here. A step: the checkpoint is done only with lefschetz-1-1-equality (decision 0004), a red-team pass, and the conventions register filled. Then take the Markman inventory.

rungs.title: Divisor–Chern identity as an exact equality on the pinned cycle class: the class of a Cartier divisor D equals the rational image of c₁(𝒪(D)), sign determined
rungs.note: Port requirement (decision 0004). The upstream branch proves this on its older cycle-class model; on the pinned model the two agree only up to a nonzero rational scalar, possibly −1 (red-team record). Prove it exactly on the pinned definitions, state the sign in the docstring, and record it in docs/conventions.md. No 'up to scalar' version counts.

rungs.title: Lefschetz (1,1) as an equality: theorem : HodgeLadder.LefschetzOneOneEquality
rungs.note: The checkpoint's definition of done (decision 0004). By lefschetzOneOneEquality_iff it is LefschetzOneOne plus CycleClassesAreHodgeOne. The latter: by divisor-chern-exact each divisor class is a first Chern class; c₁ is a d log class, so it lies in F^1; a rational class is fixed by conjugation, so it lies in conj F^1.

rungs.title: Prove the known half: theorem : HodgeLadder.CycleClassesAreHodge
rungs.note: The known half of the conjecture. With it, the upstream HodgeConjecture is equivalent to the equality Hdg^p = span, and the statement cannot hold for a degenerate reason (span accidentally everything). Classical route: a Hodge-cohomology cycle class (El Zein; Voisin2002 ch. 11) comparing cohomology with support in Z of the truncated de Rham complex with the topological class. Large; p = 1 comes first through lefschetz-1-1-equality.

rungs.title: Integral Lefschetz (1,1): the image of c₁ : Pic(X) → H²(X(ℂ); ℤ) equals the integral classes whose rational image is a Hodge class
rungs.note: The literature's form of the theorem (Lefschetz1924, GriffithsHarris1978). Upstream's proof deliberately stops at the rational span. Both inclusions are needed; torsion classes are in the image because they lie in the kernel of H²(ℤ) → H²(𝒪). Integral HC fails in higher codimension (problem.md §2), so this is the one codimension where the integral equality holds.

rungs.title: Computed test case: for projective space ℙ^n over ℂ (n ≥ 1), Hdg^1 = algebraicCycleClassSpan 1, and both are one-dimensional over ℚ
rungs.note: Pins the definitions from both sides at once: a nonzero class in degree 2, a nonzero hyperplane class, and no room for a degenerate reading. Needs H²(ℙ^n(ℂ); ℚ) ≅ ℚ on the upstream cohomology; upstream has Definitions/AlgebraicGeometry/ProjectiveSpace.lean to start from. The hyperplane-class sign is a conventions-register row.

rungs.title: The Clifford algebra of the split form on H ⊕ H^∨ acts on the exterior algebra ∧*H as its spin module, compatible with parity
rungs.note: Research note 2026-11-24 §1. For a torus A with H = H¹(A, ℚ), H*(A, ℚ) = ∧*H, so Spin(H ⊕ H^∨) acts on all of H*(A, ℚ) (Chevalley1954, Mukai1981); Markman's Weil-class construction uses this action through Orlov's equivalence. Pure linear algebra over Mathlib's CliffordAlgebra and ExteriorAlgebra; a Mathlib upstream candidate. Sequenced after the Lefschetz checkpoint.

rungs.title: Computed test: for elliptic curves E₁, E₂, dim Hdg^1(E₁ × E₂; ℚ) = 2 + rank Hom(E₁, E₂), while h^{1,1} = 4
rungs.note: Research note 2026-11-24 §3. Shows on upstream definitions that Hodge classes depend on the periods, not the Hodge diamond (dimension 2, 3 or 4). Also checks the Hodge numbers of products of elliptic curves against the refined Künneth count. Needs the cohomology of tori on upstream definitions.

rungs.title: Hard Lefschetz for the upstream rational cohomology of a smooth projective variety
rungs.note: Needs Kähler geometry and the Lefschetz decomposition on the upstream cohomology; large. Upstream and Tau Ceti have partial material; inventory before posting sub-rungs.

rungs.title: The upstream HodgeConjectureInDimensionLE 3
rungs.note: Codimension 0, 1, n-1, n; the middle cases come from Lefschetz (1,1) and hard Lefschetz (Shioda1983, daSilva2021). Target the equality form as well (decision 0004): Hdg^p = span for every p when dim X ≤ 3. Equality target: Hdg^p = algebraicCycleClassSpan X p for every p when dim X ≤ 3.

rungs.title: Markman's theorem as a solved-research statement on upstream definitions: Weil classes on abelian fourfolds of Weil type are algebraic
rungs.note: Front abelian. Deferred until the Lefschetz checkpoint (decision 0003); the inventory of tools and gaps comes from that checkpoint. Source Markman2025 is a preprint; the statement records that. Markman's method produces a sheaf whose characteristic class must equal a given Weil class with exact normalization; the statement records the normalization.
